stops.note: 'confusion, strife'; the Romance languages took this Germanic word (French guerre, Spanish guerra), perhaps because Latin bellum sounded like bellus 'pretty'
Norman kept the w- that Central French turned into gu- (guerre)
first recorded in the Peterborough Chronicle's entry for 1154, replacing native words like gūþ and wīg
the 'Hundred Years' War' (1337-1453) is a name coined by historians in the 1800s

current_meaning: armed conflict between nations or groups
